evals.prompt: The current harness is Codex. Plan a five-agent read-only review using available Codex, OpenCode, and Gemini harnesses. I did not request a roster. Return the selected harness and real configured role for each review lens; do not execute it.
evals.expected_output: A five-agent plan with three Codex workers and two best-fit external workers, using each harness's configured roles and preserving read-only review.
expectations: Allocates three of five workers to the current Codex harness
Allocates two workers to suitable available external harnesses
Uses actual configured role descriptions instead of copying Codex role names across harnesses
Keeps every specialist read-only and does not create an implicit branch or worktree
Keeps synthesis and final verification with the coordinator

evals.prompt: I have a two-line typo fix in one file. Should you launch a three-agent swarm? Explain the execution decision in at most five sentences.
evals.expected_output: Rejects a swarm because the work is small and single-owner, while preferring the current harness if one worker is still justified.
expectations: Chooses one agent rather than a swarm
Explains that coordination and token cost outweigh parallel value
Does not launch external agents merely because they are available

evals.prompt: A five-agent review was assigned as three Codex, one OpenCode, and one Gemini worker. The Codex reasoning reviewer fails at launch with an explicit quota-exhausted error. OpenCode has another configured reasoning reviewer available. Explain the recovery and final roster.
evals.expected_output: Replaces only the failed reasoning slot with the configured OpenCode reviewer, preserves its packet, and reports the final two-Codex, two-OpenCode, one-Gemini roster.
expectations: Does not retry the exhausted Codex route
Preserves the reasoning lens, read-only permission, deliverable, and evidence contract
Uses OpenCode's configured reasoning reviewer rather than a copied Codex role name
Reports the quota substitution and final harness roster
